_note: The curated cauldron-build environment: cauldron's own development, scrubbed. Owned by the soup crate (libs/soup), installed into the environment's own seed by `cauldron env create cauldron-build`.

directives.text: Faces display only what the producer reports and keep no copies of their own.
Never restart a running face without asking. Install the new build, report it, and let the reload wait.

constraints.text: Under 16 ms a frame at p99, and an empty wake costs nothing.

Read the mirror clone-free on every wake

children.name: Cauldron tab
children.description: Clusters, the bucket, the surface and the first-run states of a fresh cauldron.

directives.text: One bucket per cauldron. Dump is the verb, and the face never writes the soup itself.

constraints.text: No explanatory sentences on screen. An empty state is an action, not a paragraph.

tasks.title: First-cluster state: the + as the one action
First-environment state: create your first cauldron

questions.question: What should a fresh environment's Cauldron tab show before any ripple has run?
questions.why: A new cauldron has no clusters, no dumps and no ripples yet. The tab still has to say what to do next, without a paragraph explaining it.
options: Empty state. The + on Clusters is the one action, and the bucket still takes a dump.
Hide the tab. A fresh cauldron shows only Threads and Status until something exists.
Open the curated cauldron. A first run lands in the demo instead of an empty one.
questions.recommendation: Empty state. It keeps the tab set identical everywhere and it is honest about what is there.

closed_questions.question: Is the bucket one per cauldron or one per cluster?
closed_questions.answer: One per cauldron. Clusters are for discovery only.

children.name: Ledger
children.description: Status, Ledger: every dump that went in, its phases, and the ripples it ran, drawn as rails that fork and join.

directives.text: The ledger is cauldron-level, first under Status, and drawn like the Tasks rails.

objectives.title: A dump's whole execution is readable at a glance

milestones.handle: Ledger v1 out early for style feedback

tasks.title: Dump bands, newest first
Draw ripples on fork-and-join rails
Thread folds as their own rows

questions.question: Should a thread fold sit inline with the dumps, or in a band of its own?
questions.why: A fold is what a sidecar takes out of a Threads conversation and puts into the soup. It runs ripples like a dump does, but you did not dump it.
options: Inline. A fold is a row in time order, marked as a fold.
Own band. Folds sit under the dumps, so the dump history stays yours alone.
questions.recommendation: Inline. The ledger is the history of what ran, and a fold ran.

clusters.name: Threads daemon
clusters.description: The daemon that runs agents, keeps their event logs and shares one account pool.

directives.text: A thread's status is active, idle or error, and nothing else.

constraints.text: Never query the live store from a test or a tool.

objectives.title: Status reads the daemon's own words

milestones.handle: Every change travels as the change

tasks.title: Backpressure that coalesces and never drops
End the log wedge: one item per frame
tasks.report: A row now carries ids; bodies hydrate by id, concurrently.

questions.question: Should one account pool serve every cauldron on the machine?
questions.why: Today each environment runs its own threads daemon, so each would log in its own accounts. Builds and caches are shared; data is per environment.
options: Shared pool. Accounts are machine resources, logged in once and switched on per cauldron.
Pool per environment. Each cauldron logs in its own accounts, as the code does today.
questions.recommendation: Shared pool. One login, toggled per cauldron.

closed_questions.question: Does the face keep finished messages in memory?
closed_questions.answer: Yes, in memory only, under a cap. A sealed message can never diverge.

human_actions.ask: Make a fresh macOS user for the install proof
human_actions.body:
The install proof has to run as a user that has never seen cauldron.

## Step 1 — create the user

System Settings, Users & Groups, add a standard user.

**Deliverable:** a fresh standard account exists.

## Step 2 — log in once

Log in as that user once, so its home folder is made, then log out.

**Deliverable:** the new home folder exists.

## Step 3 — give its short name

```field
name: PROOF_USER
label: The new account's short name
secret: false
route: node
note: written back to this action's node, so the proof task can read it
```

questions.question: Should the first release carry the ripple runtime as code that cannot run yet?
questions.why: The runtime that executes a dump exists on its own branch, but nothing can land a tranche's writes yet. In the tree it would be code no one can run.
options: Ship without it. The ledger shows curated runs in the curated cauldron, and the runtime merges next week.
Ship it dormant. The code is in the tree, switched off.
questions.recommendation: Ship without it. The first release stays small and every part of it runs.

human_actions.body:
The public release needs two secrets that only you hold. Nothing you type here is shown again or written into this ticket.

## Step 1 — create a release token

Make a fine-grained token that can push to the new public repository and nothing else.

```open
url: https://github.com/settings/personal-access-tokens/new
label: Open the token page
```

**Deliverable:** a token scoped to the one repository.

## Step 2 — paste the release token

```field
name: RELEASE_TOKEN
label: Release token
route: env
note: written to this cauldron's own secrets env file, mode 0600; never into a file a repo tracks
```

## Step 3 — paste the notarization password

```field
name: NOTARY_APP_PASSWORD
label: App-specific password for notarization
route: env:NOTARY_PASSWORD
note: the same env file, under the name NOTARY_PASSWORD
```

## Step 4 — confirm the publish

Read the final file list once more, then mark this done. The publish ripple waits on it.

**Deliverable:** your go on the final contents.

Pick the license the public tree ships under.

**Deliverable:** a license chosen.

regions.handle: THE FACE - the terminal interface: tabs, clusters, the bucket and how it reads the daemon.
regions.boundary: Inside: what the face draws and how it reads it. Outside: what produces the data (the soup, the ripples, the threads daemon).

regions.handle: THE SOUP - the typed, versioned knowledge graph of one environment, and the door ripples write through.
regions.boundary: Inside: nodes, regions, tranches and the write door. Outside: which ripple decides a write (R-3).

regions.handle: RIPPLES - the runs that turn a dump into work: type one, type two and type three.
regions.boundary: Inside: ripple kinds, the dump ripple, routing and the ledger of what ran. Outside: the soup's storage (R-2).

regions.handle: THREADS - the daemon that runs agents and the account pool they share.
regions.boundary: Inside: thread status, the event log, the pool. Outside: how a face lays a thread out (R-1).

regions.handle: RELEASE - what ships: the install path, the public tree, the teaser.
regions.boundary: Inside: packaging, scrubbing, licensing, the video. Outside: the features themselves.

nodes.handle: Globs are clusters: the tree, the tab and every word on screen say cluster.
nodes.body: Folded from a dump that renamed the header; every page followed.

nodes.handle: The bucket's legend says surface; the area you type in is the bucket.
nodes.body: Folded from a dump; the old legend 'soup' is gone from the face.

nodes.handle: The demo data lives in the soup crate, never in UI code.
nodes.body: The curated environment loads it through the same seed path as any hand-curated cauldron.

nodes.handle: The log wedge: one frame carried a whole window and stalled every face.
nodes.body: A shape stored a list of rows in one cell. Fixed by sending one item per frame and hydrating by id.

nodes.handle: The idle face used most of a core doing nothing.
nodes.body: Every wake deep-copied every open window to find zero new rows. Fixed by a clone-free read; an empty wake now costs nothing.

nodes.handle: Threads read 'absent' while the daemon had them.
nodes.body: The face only subscribed status for recent threads and treated 'never asked' as 'does not exist'. Status is now subscribed for every listed thread.

build#1.text: Design note: work goes to the cauldron as a whole, not to individual agents; ripples carry it on from there.

build#2.text: Design note: a person's attention is the scarcest resource in the system, so the face puts questions in front of them and keeps logs out of the way.

build#3.text: Design note: each environment holds exactly one project, and separate cauldrons keep their data apart.

build#4.text: Design note: a new cluster is described in plain words, and a single type-one run populates it.

build#5.text: Design note: ripples set milestones and objectives; directives and constraints come from the person who owns the cauldron.

build#6.text: Design note: each environment has one bucket and one soup. Input arrives as a dump, and a ripple handles it.

build#7.text: Design note: faces keep no copies of data; the producer stays authoritative so the system can span several devices.

build#8.text: Release rule: a new face build is installed and announced, never forced; a running face reloads only when its user decides.

build#9.text: Design note: the soup is written only by ripples. The dump ripple stays fast and hands the real work off as queued tasks.

build#10.text: Design note: the ledger sits at cauldron level, at the top of Status, drawn like the Tasks rails, with branches splitting off and rejoining.

build#11.text: Release note: a rough first release is acceptable; finishing it matters more than polishing it.

build#12.text: Design note: a secret action is a human action whose input is masked; an adapter delivers the value to a graph node, a secret store or an env file.

build#13.text: Release rule: the first release targets macOS only, and the install path carries no personal details.

build#14.text: Design note: every thread shows exactly one of three states (active, idle, error), and always shows one.
